title: v0 baseline
hypothesis: Initial concept-based engine (see LOG.md v0 entry)
explanation: Concept-sum eval with faithfulness invariant; negamax + TT + quiescence + null move; no LMR/PVS yet.

title: String-free eval fast path
hypothesis: Profile showed 68% of search time in eval: piece_map dict building and f-string detail lists on the hot path. Bitboard-based EvalContext + numeric score() should give a large NPS gain.
explanation: EvalContext built from bitboards (no dicts); pawn structure, king safety, piece activity score numerically instead of summing their labeled details. Faithfulness tests guarantee fast and detailed paths stay identical. +19% NPS.

title: Qsearch capture generation
hypothesis: Quiescence materializes the full legal move list at every node just to filter captures; generate_legal_captures() avoids that.
explanation: generate_legal_captures() plus explicit non-capturing queen promotions replaces generate-all-and-filter in quiescence. +13% NPS.

title: Pawn-keyed eval caches
hypothesis: Pawn structure depends only on the two pawn bitboards, king safety on pawns + king squares (linearly scaled by phase); both cache with high hit rates inside a search tree.
explanation: Phase-free components cached by pawn/king bitboard keys, phase applied at use. details() recomputes from scratch so the explanation path stays exact. +7% NPS.

title: Late move reductions
hypothesis: With decent move ordering, quiet moves late in the list rarely change the result; searching them 2 plies shallower (re-search on surprise) buys depth.
explanation: Quiet moves ordered 5th+ at depth>=3 (not in check) searched at depth-2 with a null window, full re-search if they beat alpha. Avg depth 7.0 -> 8.2; the extra depth solved the last tactics position (24/24).

title: Principal variation search
hypothesis: Null-window scout searches for non-first moves cut nodes when move ordering is good.
explanation: First move full window, later moves scouted with (alpha, alpha+1), re-search on scout fail-high. 421k -> 411k nodes to depth 6 (-2.4%), -4.5% wall time.

title: Aspiration windows
hypothesis: A +/-50cp root window around the previous iteration score should cut nodes via earlier cutoffs.
explanation: +0.8% nodes at +/-50, -0.2% at +/-100 — within noise. Iteration-to-iteration score swings with this eval regularly exceed the window, so re-searches eat the savings. Reverted; revisit after eval tuning stabilizes root scores.

title: Futility pruning
hypothesis: At frontier nodes (depth<=2, not in check), quiet non-checking moves are hopeless when static eval + margin can't reach alpha.
explanation: Margins 150cp (depth 1) / 300cp (depth 2), at least one move always searched. 411k -> 253k nodes to depth 6 (-38%), -16% wall time to fixed depth; tactics 24/24. NPS reads lower because pruned subtrees were the cheapest nodes; time-to-depth is what improved.

title: Strength gate: match vs v0 baseline
hypothesis: The accepted search/speed changes (exps 1-5, 7) translate into real playing strength, measured by a 20-game match vs the v0 engine at 0.3s/move.
explanation: +11 =7 -2 (72.5%) over 20 games across 10 openings, both colors: about +168 Elo over v0 (95% CI roughly +20..+425). Also surfaced and fixed a real bug: search could return no move when depth 1 didn't complete in time, sending an illegal null move in games. Absolute anchor: +5 =1 -4 (55%) over 10 games vs strength-limited Stockfish 1400 at 0.3s/move -> roughly 1435 Elo absolute (wide CI at 10 games).

title: Session 2: eval-accuracy loop (32 experiments)
hypothesis: A fast proxy metric (static-eval accuracy vs Stockfish, win-prob MSE) enables Karpathy-style rapid iteration on the evaluation.
explanation: 32 experiments at ~0.5s cycle time. Metric screened 5 good new concepts (king attack, safe mobility, blockaded passers, bad bishop, graded shield) and honestly rejected 4. Headline negative result: optimizing weights against the metric was anti-correlated with strength (fully-tuned engine ~-130 Elo vs session-1 despite -15% val loss). Adopted exp-13 state: new concepts at chess-prior weights, 55% vs session-1. See session2.json + session2_report.html.

title: Session 3: metric research + move-ranking loop + contrastive explanations
hypothesis: A metric validated against match-measured strength (sibling-rank agreement) iterates fast without session-2's anti-correlation; explanations should contrast the chosen move with the runner-up.
explanation: Meta-experiment picked rank agreement (monotone with strength across 4 match-measured states; evalloss anti-correlated, move-match noisy). Loop: threats concept adopted at 0.1x after passing its match gate (55%); the metric's preferred 0.6x scored 5% in the gate (~-500 Elo), confirming the rule that fast metrics screen concepts while matches set magnitudes. Speed: shared attack masks + bitmask threats (+15% NPS). Interpretability: contrastive explanations (why this move over the runner-up) with faithfulness tests.

title: Session 4: divergence mining + SF ladder + Elo timeline
hypothesis: Positions where our eval diverges most from Stockfish point at fixable weaknesses; a multi-level ladder gives a solid absolute Elo anchor.
explanation: Divergence miner found the dominant error motif (center-stuck kings under attack) but all three targeted static terms failed both metrics honestly - this class needs search, not eval terms. 60-game SF ladder: 1773 Elo (1668-1886); session-1 state re-anchored at ~1737 on the same scale, consistent with head-to-head deltas. GUI: square colors fixed, moves tab, eval graph, gated eval bar. Elo timeline: research/elo_report.html.

title: Session 5: search sprint (SEE, LMR tiers, eval cache, qsearch checks)
hypothesis: Search depth/quality is the highest-confidence Elo lever (sessions 1-4 evidence).
explanation: 7 experiments, 6 kept: transposition-keyed eval cache (-19% time), adaptive null-move R (-13% nodes at d7), two LMR tiers (-28%), SEE pruning/ordering in qsearch (-29%), qsearch evasions + first-ply quiet checks (gate 55%). Net 15.56s -> 9.88s to depth 6 with better tactical quality. Batch gate vs session-4: +9 =5 -6 (57.5%, ~+53 Elo). New ladder anchor: 1850 (1737-1963) over 40 games vs SF 1700-2000.

title: Session 6: opening book (+ SPRT tooling, pruning dead-ends)
hypothesis: More search strength via pruning; if that fails, an interpretable opening book is a safe practical-Elo gain.
explanation: Pruning (reverse futility, late-move pruning) all passed the deterministic time-to-depth metric but lost their match gates (42%/29%/40% vs session-5) — the metric rewards node-cutting regardless of strength, and static-eval pruning hurts an engine with a deliberately simple eval. Reverted. The win: a 250-position curated opening book (interpretable, 'Book move: Ruy Lopez'), which gated at +20=2-8 (70%, +147 Elo). New ladder anchor 2018 (1905-2134). Added SPRT early-stopping to the match harness.

title: Session 7: endgame technique (mating drive)
hypothesis: Fix concrete endgame conversion weaknesses found by a diagnostic, interpretably.
explanation: Diagnostic: KBB/KBN vs K were unconvertable (50-move draws), a won KPvK was lost. Added a 'mating drive' concept (drive enemy king to corner + bring own king up) active only in bare-king endgames -> KBB mate in 67 plies, KBN in 79. Provably neutral outside bare-king endgames (0 on all non-lone-king positions), so no gate needed. Negative results: KPvK bitbase dropped (correctness rabbit hole, tiny Elo); book expansion 250->478 gate-rejected at 36% (-98 Elo) because added sharp lines don't suit the simple eval. Engine stays ~2018 Elo but converts basic mates it was drawing.

title: Compiled core (C engine) — the big strength jump
hypothesis: A compiled core (move gen + search + eval mirroring Python exactly) breaks the pure-Python plateau while preserving interpretability.
explanation: Ported board+movegen+search+eval to C (clang->dylib, ctypes). Perft matches python-chess exactly (43x faster movegen). C eval == Python eval to 0.000000 on 6204 positions (interpretability guarantee: fast search optimizes exactly what the explanation shows). C search reaches depth 9 vs Python's 4 at 1s. Head-to-head: +24=6-0 (90%, +382 Elo) vs the ~2018 Python engine. Ladder-anchored at 2442 (2305-2582). Python explanation layer unchanged and still exact.

title: Session 10 exp1: incremental Zobrist hashing
hypothesis: Recomputing Board.hash from scratch at every negamax node is wasteful; maintain it incrementally in make() (XOR only what changed), with a hash-free make_light() for legality-test copies.
explanation: 1.28->1.22s to depth 9 (-5%); node count BYTE-IDENTICAL (1,401,527) so search shape unchanged (no match gate, like the s5 eval cache). make_light() added because gen_legal()'s throwaway copies were paying for hash upkeep they never use (first attempt was slower). Perft unchanged, 350k+ hash-verify positions zero mismatches, eval cross-check 0.000000, 46 tests pass.

title: Session 10 exp2: SEE-based capture ordering in the main search
hypothesis: Ordering captures by static-exchange value (real material outcome), demoting losing captures below quiet history, beats MVV-LVA even though it costs SEE compute per node.
explanation: Deterministic metric said NO (+5% time / +7% nodes to depth 9), but the match said YES: +15 =39 -6 (58%, +53 Elo, 95% -35..+147) over 60 games at 0.3s/move vs the pre-SEE core. 15 wins vs 6 losses. Ordering quality beats raw node count; the match is ground truth. Estimated ladder position ~2495 (2442 + 53 head-to-head; fresh SF re-anchor pending).

title: Session 11 exp1: search-quality v2 batch (LMR log table + history malus + countermove)
hypothesis: Three standard search-quality upgrades (aggressive log-log LMR table, history gravity, countermove heuristic) batched and gated together add strength on the C core.
explanation: Gate vs session-10 HEAD: +6 =43 -11 (46%), -29 Elo (95% -121..+59), SPRT H0 after 60 games. Suspect: LMR reductions of 4-5 plies on late quiets discard too much at depth ~10-12 (same shape as the RFP/LMP rejections). Screens (tactics, tests, nodes-to-depth) all passed - only the match caught it. Diff preserved in research/searchv2.patch; ablation of the ordering-only half gating next.

title: Session 11 exp2: history malus + countermove ordering (ablation of the v2 batch)
hypothesis: The ordering-quality half of the rejected batch (history gravity + countermove) is positive on its own with the baseline LMR tiers.
explanation: Gate vs session-10 HEAD: +11 =44 -5 (55%, +35 Elo, 95% -53..+128), 60 games at 0.3s/move. Confirms the batch's -29 came from the aggressive LMR table (~-60 implied). Chained estimate ~2530 (2442 anchor +53 SEE +35 this); fresh ladder anchor queued.

title: Session 11 exps 3-6: byte-identical speed batch (eval hash, qsearch capture gen, light check test, lazy legality)
hypothesis: The C search recomputes eval and pays full legality/make bookkeeping it can skip; each fix is provably shape-neutral (identical node counts), so time-to-depth gains are pure Elo at fixed movetime.
explanation: Four KEPT speedups, each with cttd nodes EXACTLY 3,418,463 (byte-identical search): eval hash by Board.hash (-4%), captures-only generation in deep qsearch (-7%), quiet-check test on a make_light copy (-2%), lazy legality on an up-front-ordered pseudo list (-10%; first-move cutoffs skip ~35 legality tests). Net 3.12->2.46s (-21%). Benchmark ~2.0M NPS. Perft, eval cross-check, 46 tests, tactics all green.

title: Session 11 ladder re-anchor: 2529 Elo
hypothesis: The chained estimate (~2530 = 2442 + 53 SEE + 35 countermove) matches a fresh direct SF-ladder measurement.
explanation: 30 games vs SF 2400/2600/2800 at 0.3s/move: 60%/50%/15%. MLE 2529 (2388-2666) vs chained ~2530 -- agreement within 1 Elo validates both. Anchored post speed-batch (the -21% time matters at fixed movetime).

title: Session 11 exp7: magic bitboards — the second-biggest speed win
hypothesis: slide()'s ray loops (under in_check, SEE, movegen, eval mobility) dominate per-node cost; magic-bitboard lookups are byte-identical and much faster.
explanation: Magics found at init (seeded, deterministic, <0.5s); tables built FROM slide() and verified injective, so attack sets identical by construction. cttd 2.46->1.79s (-28%); session speed total 3.12->1.79s (-43%), all byte-identical. Benchmark 3.76M NPS (2.04M pre-magics). Perft, eval 0.000000, 46 tests, tactics 24/24. NOTE: landed after the 2529 anchor; next anchor captures it.

title: Session 11 exp8: is_legal() bitboard-surgery legality test
hypothesis: make_light (20% of profile) can be eliminated: legality only needs post-move attack probes from the king square.
explanation: Direct bitboard surgery (occ2, captured-piece removal, magic lookups from king sq) replaces copy+make_light+in_check at all legality sites. Perft exact, nodes byte-identical, 1.79->1.61s. Session speed total 3.12->1.61s (-48%).

title: Session 11 exp9: lazy best-move selection
hypothesis: On-demand max-pick beats a full sort at cutoff nodes.
explanation: Byte-identical (orig-index tie-break) but zero time gain: sorting isn't the hot part of order() (see/history scoring is) and illegal moves each newly paid an O(n) pick scan. Reverted for simplicity.
